purposes.src/didact/createElement.js: What JSX compiles to: a plain `{ type, props }` object, with the children inside `props`.
purposes.src/didact/dom.js: Two jobs on a single DOM node: build it from an element, and bring its properties and listeners in line with new props.
purposes.src/didact/renderSync.js: A first draft of `render`: recurse through the tree and append nodes as you go. Assignment 4 replaces it with a work loop. The file stays for comparison.
purposes.src/didact/state.js: Shared bookkeeping in one object: what to work on next, and the tree under construction. It has to be an object, because an ES module can't share a variable for other modules to reassign.
purposes.src/didact/render.js: `render` and the work loop behind it: one fiber per unit of work, and the browser can interrupt between units.
purposes.src/didact/reconcile.js: Decides which fibers a parent's children become. At first that means a fresh fiber for every child, then a comparison with the previous render.
purposes.src/didact/index.js: What an app imports: one `Didact` object carrying `createElement` and `render`, with the hooks joining it as you write them.
purposes.src/didact/commit.js: Applies a finished fiber tree to the DOM in a single pass, which keeps half a render from ever showing.
purposes.src/didact/hooks.js: State and effects that belong to a component and outlive its re-renders, stored on the fiber: `useState` and `useEffect`.
purposes.src/app/TodoApp.js: A todo list written the way an application would write it, as function components on your own Didact.
purposes.src/main.js: Where the finished program starts: it mounts the todo app into the page's `#root`.

book.title: Build React yourself

sources.title: Creating Our Own React From Scratch
sources.author: Wim Jongeneel

book.author: Rodrigo Pombo
book.headline: Learn what React does by writing it
book.lede: Rebuild React's core in JavaScript: elements, a work loop over fibers, the commit phase, reconciliation by position and by key, function components, useState, useEffect, and a todo app running on your own library. Your code runs on a small DOM, and what it draws is compared with real React 19.3.1 on jsdom. Where the two posts this follows differ from React as it is today, the tests follow React.
book.credits: Expected outputs come from React 19.3.1 running on jsdom 30.1.3, with small independent models covering the counts of work. The book saves your progress in this browser and nowhere else.

jobs.assignments/assignment_01_create_element: This is the test wiring, finished in the Boilerplate: it hands your `createElement` to the harness, which calls it and writes down what it returns. From scratch it is three lines, described at the end of the page.
jobs.src/didact/createElement.js: Write `createElement(type, props, ...children)`, which returns the element `{ type, props }` with every child inside `props.children`, and `createTextElement(text)`, which wraps a string or number as the text element that goes there.

jobs.assignments/assignment_02_dom_props.js: Test wiring, finished in the Boilerplate: it hands your `createDom` and `updateDom` to the tests, so there is nothing to design. From scratch it is three lines: import `createDom` and `updateDom` from `../src/didact/dom.js`, import `runScenarioFile` from `../harness/scenario.js`, and end with `await runScenarioFile(process.argv[2], process.argv[3], { createDom, updateDom })`.
jobs.src/didact/dom.js: Write `createDom(element)`, which builds the DOM node for an element, and `updateDom(dom, prevProps, nextProps)`, which changes a node from one set of props to the next and writes only what differs: new and changed properties are set, removed ones are cleared, and a listener is swapped when its handler changed.

jobs.assignments/assignment_03_first_render.j: Hand `runScenarioFile` the `render` from `renderSync.js`. The scenario renders a tree and dumps the container.
jobs.src/didact/renderSync.js: Implement `render(element, container)`: build the DOM for the element and for each child below it, and append the result to the container.

jobs.assignments/assignment_04_fibers.js: Run `runScenarioFile` with your `Didact` object. The scenario renders a tree, runs idle periods of a size it picks, and dumps the container.
jobs.src/didact/state.js: Create one `state` object to hold the next unit of work and the root of the tree being built.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Build `render`, `workLoop` and `performUnitOfWork`. `render` only schedules the work; each idle period then runs fibers, one per unit of work, until `timeRemaining()` falls below 1.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Give every element a fiber of its own in `reconcileChildren(wipFiber, elements)`, and link the fibers with `child`, `sibling` and `parent`.

jobs.assignments/assignment_05_commit.js: Wire your `Didact` object into `runScenarioFile`; the scenario dumps the container between idle periods.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Define `commitRoot` and `commitWork`. Once the last unit is done, they append the finished tree to the container in a single pass.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Stop attaching DOM nodes while units run. Hold the tree under construction in `wipRoot`, and call `commitRoot` after the last unit.

jobs.assignments/assignment_06_reconcile.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`. The scenario renders a second tree into the container that already holds the first.
jobs.src/didact/state.js: Track the last tree you committed in `currentRoot`, and the fibers waiting for removal in `deletions`.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: On every `render`, point the new root's `alternate` at `currentRoot` (the tree you committed last time) and reset `deletions`.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Rewrite `reconcileChildren` to compare each element with the old fiber at the same position. The same type keeps its DOM node and gets updated, a different type gets a fresh node, and an old fiber left without an element is queued for deletion.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Carry out what reconciliation decided. A new node goes before the next sibling that already has a DOM node, which keeps its position; an updated one goes through `updateDom`; each deleted node is removed once.

jobs.assignments/assignment_07_keys.js: Point `runScenarioFile` at your `Didact` object. The scenario re-renders lists whose children carry keys.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Pair each child with the old child that has the same `key`, wherever that one stood, as long as the keys both lists share stay in the same order. Children without a key still match by position.

jobs.assignments/assignment_08_reorder.js: Feed `runScenarioFile` your `Didact` object and let the scenario shuffle keyed lists.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Let a key keep matching its old child when the shared keys come in a different order.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Move the DOM node of a reordered child instead of recreating it; a node that lives on keeps its state.

jobs.assignments/assignment_09_function_compo: Use `runScenarioFile` with your `Didact` object to render trees that contain the catalog's function components.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Teach `performUnitOfWork` about fibers whose type is a function: they have no DOM node, and their children are whatever calling the function returns.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Teach `commitWork` and the removal code about fibers that have no DOM node. The DOM parent to append into, and the DOM node to remove, can each be more than one fiber away.

jobs.assignments/assignment_10_use_state.js: Your `Didact` object goes to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario clicks buttons in catalog components and dumps the result.
jobs.src/didact/hooks.js: Give function components memory with `useState(initial)`, keeping the state on the fiber and finding it again on the next render by hook index. The setter takes an updater function, queues it and schedules a new render from the root.
jobs.src/didact/state.js: Add `wipFiber` and `hookIndex`. The first is the fiber of the component being rendered, the second the position of the next hook call.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Before a function component is called, point `wipFiber` at its fiber, give that fiber an empty `hooks` array and reset `hookIndex`.

jobs.assignments/assignment_11_use_effect.js: Send your `Didact` object through `runScenarioFile`. The scenario mounts, updates and removes catalog components that log from their effects.
jobs.src/didact/hooks.js: Write `useEffect(effect, deps)`: store the effect on its fiber, along with its dependencies and whatever cleanup function the effect returned.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Once the DOM is up to date, run the cleanups of effects that run again, then the effects that are new or whose dependencies changed. A removed component's cleanups run too.
jobs.src/didact/index.js: Export `useEffect` on the `Didact` object next to `useState`.

jobs.assignments/assignment_12_todo_app.js: Supply `runScenarioFile` with your `Didact` object and your `TodoApp`. The scenario types into the form, adds items, toggles and removes them.
jobs.src/app/TodoApp.js: Compose `TodoApp` from function components on your Didact: a form with a controlled input, a list of keyed items, and a toggle and a remove button on each item.
jobs.src/main.js: Mount `TodoApp` into the page's `#root`; `index.html` then shows a working app.

requires: react, react-dom and jsdom, only for fresh test sets (npm install in tools/oracle)
